author: Nineteenth century videos. Back to life.
description:
Step into the very dawn of cinematic humor. This 1896 short captures one of the earliest examples of "slapstick" comedy: the tale of a fake blind man, and a lady in her finest dress in a prank that ends in a messy disaster.

In an era where moving pictures were a miracle, these simple sketches brought joy to the first cinema audiences. Watching it today in full color, we can appreciate the physical acting and the genuine reactions of a world experimenting with storytelling for the very first time. The ruined dress and the mischievous "blind" man remind us that while fashion changes, our sense of humor is timeless.

Can you imagine the surprise of the audiences seeing this for the first time in 1896? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

Music: Sonata No. 1 in D Minor, Op. 75, Camille Saint-Saëns
title: (1896, 4K, 60fps) First comedies ever filmed
